content: Each lapse is like the letting fall of a ball of string which one is carefully winding up; a single slip undoes more than a great many turns will wind again.
author: William James
story:
This insight touches directly on the messy reality of human nature. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

Across his life and work, William James saw how easily we surrender our tranquility to fear, vanity, and distraction. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: What hidden motive, insecurity, or fear might be silently driving your recent reactions?
